'''Cody Allen Zeller''' (born October 5, 1992) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played high school basketball at [[Washington High School (Washington, Indiana)|Washington High School]] in [[Washington, Indiana]], where he was named [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] as a senior in 2011.

Zeller played two seasons of college basketball for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] from 2011 to 2013. During his freshman season, he was named [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] and part of the All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] second team. In his sophomore season, he was named as a second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and part of the All-Big Ten first team.

Zeller was selected fourth overall in the 2013 NBA draft by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]], who rebranded to the Hornets a year later. As a rookie, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]]. Following eight seasons with the Hornets, he signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in August 2021, whom he spent one season with. Zeller joined the [[Miami Heat]] in February 2023, with whom he reached the 2023 [[NBA Finals]]. He then signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in July 2023.

===Freshman season===

In Zeller's first year as a Hoosier during the [[2011–12 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2011–12 season]] he led the team with 15.6 points and 6.6 rebounds per game while shooting 62.3 percent (200-of-321) from the field and 75.5 percent (163-of-216) from the free-throw line.<ref name="Corazza">{{cite news|last=Corazza|first=Ryan|title=That's a Wrap: Cody Zeller|url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2012/04/09/thats-a-wrap-cody-zeller/|access-date=April 9, 2012|newspaper=Inside the Hall|date=April 9, 2012|archive-date=April 11, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120411235840/http://www.insidethehall.com/2012/04/09/thats-a-wrap-cody-zeller/|url-status=live}}</ref> He ranked fourth in the country in field goal percentage, led the [[Big Ten Conference]] and posted the second-highest percentage in school history.<ref name="IUPressRelease">{{cite news|title=Watford, Zeller Will Be Back For Indiana Men's Basketball|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041012aab.html|access-date=April 10, 2012|newspaper=Indiana Univ Athletic Dept|date=April 10, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120413234642/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041012aab.html|archive-date=April 13, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> His offensive rating of 126.8 ranked him 14th nationwide. Zeller was the Big Ten's Freshman of the Year, as voted on by the coaches, after earning Big Ten Freshman of the Week seven times.<ref>{{cite web|title=Zeller named Big Ten Freshman of the Year|url=http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030512aaf.html|access-date=March 25, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120311014227/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030512aaf.html|archive-date=March 11, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also Second Team All-Big Ten and a First Team Freshman All-American. He was a finalist for the Wayman Tisdale Award (USBWA National Freshman of the Year) and was a candidate for the John Wooden Award and Oscar Robertson Trophy.<ref name="IUPressRelease"/>

===Sophomore season===
Although projected to be a top ten pick in the [[2012 NBA draft]], Zeller decided to return for his sophomore season at Indiana, along with teammate [[Christian Watford]]. In a statement issued by the Indiana Athletic Department, he said, "I grew up hoping that one day I would get the opportunity to play in the NBA, but at this point, I'm not ready for my college experience to be over...My college experience at IU this year has exceeded my expectations, on and off the court."<ref name="IUPressRelease"/>

Due in part to Zeller's leadership, the Indiana Hoosiers finished the [[2012–13 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|2012–13 season]] as the outright Big Ten champions. He finished the regular season as the conference's third-highest scorer (16.8 points) and second highest rebounder (8.2), along with second in the league in shooting at 57% while only trailing teammate Victor Oladipo in the Big Ten.<ref name="2013awards">{{cite web | url=http://indiana.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1482278 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411173843/http://indiana.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1482278 | url-status=dead | archive-date=April 11, 2013 | title=Oladipo, Zeller head IU Big 10 honorees | publisher=Rivals.com | access-date=March 12, 2013 | author=Rabjohns, Jeff }}</ref>

Zeller accumulated numerous post-season awards. He was named a [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2013 All-American]] by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] (2nd Team) and ''[[Sporting News]]'' (3rd Team). He was also named First Team All-Big Ten by both the coaches and media, as well as a First Team Academic All-American.

At the end of his sophomore season, Zeller decided to enter the [[2013 NBA draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9155252/indiana-hoosiers-cody-zeller-leaving-nba-draft-report-says |title=Cody Zeller entering 2013 NBA draft |access-date=July 15, 2024 |archive-date=November 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127052516/https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9155252/indiana-hoosiers-cody-zeller-leaving-nba-draft-report-says |url-status=live }}</ref> along with teammate [[Victor Oladipo]].

[[File:Cody Zeller (31538663811).jpg|thumb|Zeller with the Hornets in December 2016]]
Zeller was selected with the fourth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-select-cody-zeller-fourth-pick-2013-nba-draft |title=Bobcats Select Cody Zeller With Fourth Pick in 2013 NBA Draft |work=NBA.com |date=June 27, 2013 |access-date=July 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701061735/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-select-cody-zeller-fourth-pick-2013-nba-draft |archive-date=July 1, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On July 10, 2013, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Bobcats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobcats Sign 2013 First-Round Draft Pick Cody Zeller |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/bobcats-sign-2013-first-round-draft-pick-cody-zeller |access-date=March 12, 2022 |website=NBA |archive-date=February 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230221161307/https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/bobcats-sign-2013-first-round-draft-pick-cody-zeller |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 31, 2014, he scored a season-high 15 points against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref name="br1314">{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zelleco01/gamelog/2014/ |title=Cody Zeller 2013-14 Game Log |access-date=December 3, 2017 |archive-date=February 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180208192104/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zelleco01/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 5, 2014, he recorded his first career double-double with 12 points and 11 rebounds against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="br1314" /> He appeared in all 82 regular season games and all four of Charlotte's playoff games.<ref name="br1314" /> At the season's end, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidethehall.com/2014/05/22/oladipo-zeller-earn-nba-rookie-honors/ |title=Oladipo, Zeller earn NBA All-Rookie honors |access-date=May 27, 2014 |archive-date=May 28, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528005211/http://www.insidethehall.com/2014/05/22/oladipo-zeller-earn-nba-rookie-honors/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/22/michael-carter-williams-leads-2013-14-nba-all-rookie-team-selections/ |title=Sixers' Carter-Williams leads 2013-14 All-Rookie Team picks |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140603020903/http://www.nba.com/2014/news/05/22/michael-carter-williams-leads-2013-14-nba-all-rookie-team-selections/ |archive-date=June 3, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 28, 2014, Zeller recorded 15 points and 14 rebounds against the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref name=br1415>{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zelleco01/gamelog/2015/ |title=Cody Zeller 2014-15 Game Log |access-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-date=November 29, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181129100439/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zelleco01/gamelog/2015/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On January 31, 2015, he scored a season-high 21 points in a 104–86 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref name="br1415" /><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150131/CHADEN/gameinfo.html |title=Cody Zeller scores 21, Hornets rout Nuggets 104-86 |access-date=February 1, 2015 |archive-date=February 4, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150204060943/http://www.nba.com/games/20150131/CHADEN/gameinfo.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022)===
On August 4, 2021, Zeller signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN CODY ZELLER|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/8/4/trail-blazers-sign-cody-zeller|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2021|access-date=August 4, 2021|archive-date=November 6, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221106215605/https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2021/8/4/trail-blazers-sign-cody-zeller|url-status=live}}</ref> He was waived on February 8, 2022, to make room for players acquired in the [[CJ McCollum]] trade.<ref>{{Cite press release|date=February 8, 2022|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|title=TRAIL BLAZERS COMPLETE TRADE WITH NEW ORLEANS|publisher=Portland Trail Blazers|quote=In a related move, the Trail Blazers have waived Cody Zeller.|access-date=February 9, 2022|archive-date=February 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215022547/https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-complete-trade-new-orleans|url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 25, 2022, Zeller signed with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Cody Zeller|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-cody-zeller|website=NBA.com|date=September 25, 2022|access-date=September 26, 2022|archive-date=October 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014144445/https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-cody-zeller|url-status=live}}</ref> On October 15, he was waived.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title=Jazz Waive Former High Draft Pick, Set Final Roster |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/jazz-waive-jared-butler-cody-zeller |access-date=January 22, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=October 15, 2022 |archive-date=January 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122171439/https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/jazz-waive-jared-butler-cody-zeller |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Miami Heat (2023)===
On February 20, 2023, Zeller signed with the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT Sign Cody Zeller |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-cody-zeller |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 20, 2023 |archive-date=February 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230221004042/https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-cody-zeller |url-status=live }}</ref> The eighth-seeded Heat would embark on a [[Underdog#Cinderella|Cinderella run]] through the playoffs, culminating in an Eastern Conference championship. In his tenth season, Zeller reached the [[2023 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the first time in his career. The Heat would ultimately fall to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in five games.

===New Orleans Pelicans (2023–2024)===
On July 6, 2023, Zeller signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/cody-zeller-center-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-nba-free-agency-2023|title=Pelicans sign Cody Zeller|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 6, 2023|archive-date=July 14, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230714132251/https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/cody-zeller-center-new-orleans-pelicans-roster-nba-free-agency-2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 6, 2024, Zeller, [[Larry Nance Jr.]], [[E. J. Liddell]], [[Dyson Daniels]], a 2025 first-round pick (via Lakers), and a conditional 2027 first-round pick were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Dejounte Murray]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Acquire Dyson Daniels, E.J. Liddell, Larry Nance Jr., Cody Zeller, and 2 Future First-Round Draft Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-dyson-daniels-e-j-liddell-larry-nance-jr-cody-zeller-and-2-future-first-round-draft-picks|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024|archive-date=July 7, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240707004053/https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-acquire-dyson-daniels-e-j-liddell-larry-nance-jr-cody-zeller-and-2-future-first-round-draft-picks|url-status=live}}</ref> Zeller was acquired via a sign-and-trade deal.

On February 6, 2025, Zeller and a 2028 second-round pick were traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Alpha Kaba]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-trade-with-atlanta|title=Rockets Complete Trade With Atlanta|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2025}}</ref>

On March 2, 2025, Cody Zeller was waived by the [[Houston Rockets]] to create roster space for guard [[Nate Williams (basketball, born 1999)|Nate Williams]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Stinar |first=Ben |title=Houston Rockets Make Roster Move Before Thunder Game |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/houston-rockets-make-roster-move-before-thunder-game-williams-zeller-nba-news |date=March 2, 2025 |access-date=March 3, 2025 |archive-date=March 3, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250303135248/https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/houston-rockets-make-roster-move-before-thunder-game-williams-zeller-nba-news |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Player profile==
In college, analysts described Zeller's "mobility, scoring instincts, and aggressiveness" as particularly noteworthy.<ref name="Givony">{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |date=December 8, 2011 |title=NBA Draft Prospect of the Week: Cody Zeller |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Cody-Zeller-6241/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130621234134/http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Cody-Zeller-6241 |archive-date=June 21, 2013 |access-date=April 7, 2012 |publisher=DraftExpress}}</ref> Zeller is also known for a "high basketball IQ" and unselfish play.<ref name="ESPN"/>

==Personal life==
Zeller is from [[Washington, Indiana]] and the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]]. He is the youngest brother of former [[North Carolina Tar Heels|North Carolina]] and NBA center [[Tyler Zeller]] and former [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]] and [[Phoenix Suns]] forward-center [[Luke Zeller]].<ref>[http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_cody00.html Cody Zeller Bio – IUHOOSIERS.COM] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130904170215/http://www.iuhoosiers.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_cody00.html |date=September 4, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Miller |first=Sam |date=October 19, 2011 |title=Hoops Runs Through Luke Zeller's Family Tree |url=http://archive.usab.com/mens/panamerican/11_mpag_zeller_feature.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084427/http://archive.usab.com/mens/panamerican/11_mpag_zeller_feature.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=January 14, 2016 |work=usab.com}}</ref> Despite pressures brought on by unusually high expectations, commentators have noted his humility and work ethic, along with "dry wit and prankster's mirth."<ref>O'Neil, Dana. (December 1, 2012). [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7442851/unassuming-cody-zeller-keys-indiana-hoosiers-turnaround-college-basketball "Cody Zeller sparks Hoosiers' turnaround"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417083624/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/7442851/unassuming-cody-zeller-keys-indiana-hoosiers-turnaround-college-basketball |date=April 17, 2023 }}. ''ESPN''. Retrieved June 7, 2015.</ref> In May 2017, Zeller earned his bachelor's degree when he graduated from [[Indiana University]]'s [[Kelley School of Business]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Wilco|first1=Daniel|title=Cody Zeller graduates from Indiana four years after leaving for the NBA Draft|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2017-05-06/cody-zeller-graduates-indiana-four-years-after-leaving-nba|website=NCAA.com|access-date=May 7, 2017|date=May 6, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Spears|first1=Joseph|title=Cody Zeller graduates four years after leaving Indiana|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2017/05/06/cody-zeller-graduates-four-years-after-leaving-indiana/101383394/|website=Indianapolis Star|access-date=May 7, 2017|date=May 6, 2017}}</ref>

He married Contemporary Christian recording artist, [[Leanna Crawford]], in 2023.
